## setting
**94 run(s)** — rule `lappe-setting` — 10.1186/s12864-022-09001-w  
*Supplementary Table 1, Line column cross-tabulated against Area*

> The Line column distinguishes wild from planted material and the cross-tabulation is unambiguous. All 21 samples labelled 'wild teosinte population' (Zea mays ssp mexicana) sit in Area 3 with coordinates: these are wild stands, so they take setting = field (natural population). All 34 numbered germplasm accessions (6013-1, 6124-1, 6046-1 style, annotated lowland/highland/Nicaraguan/perennial teosinte) sit in Area 1 with coordinates, which makes them seed-bank lines PLANTED in a field plot rather than wild collections, so they take plain field. The remaining Mexican samples are named maize lines, landraces, 'unknown maize', 'cultivated hybrid' and four from an 'abandoned cornfield'. The 3 Aphids rows are 'Live shipped from Jander' - lab-reared insects from Ithaca, not plant tissue and not field.

## sampling_selection
**94 run(s)** — rule `lappe-sampling_selection` — 10.1186/s12864-022-09001-w  
*Materials and methods, 'RNA extraction, cDNA library preparation, and RNA sequencing'*

> 'The DNA-free total RNA was subjected to ribosomal RNA depletion by Illumina Ribo-Zero rRNA Removal Kit (Plant Leaf) ... Strand-specific cDNA libraries were prepared from ribosomal depleted RNA using the NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA Library Prep kit.' THIS IS THE ONLY RIBODEPLETED PROJECT IN THE COHORT; every other is polyA-selected. A ribodepleted library retains non-polyadenylated and bacterial transcripts that polyA selection removes, so the microbial FRACTION of reads is systematically higher here for reasons of chemistry rather than biology. Fungal mRNA is polyadenylated and captured by both methods, so these runs remain usable for fungal detection, but any comparison expressed as a percentage of classified reads is invalid against the rest of the cohort. CLAUDE.md's existing rule - report read counts, not percentages - is what makes them safe to include. The archive's library_selection reads 'cDNA' on all 151 and does not distinguish the chemistries.

## tissue
**94 run(s)** — rule `lappe-tissue` — 10.1186/s12864-022-09001-w  
*Materials and methods, 'Plant material'*

> The majority of maize and teosinte leaf samples were collected in the state of Guanajuato, Mexico, in areas between and surrounding the cities of Irapuato and Moroleon. Approximately 20 cm long leaf tips from mature maize plants were collected with scissors in October, 2017. Individual leaves were placed into 50 mL screw-cap centrifuge tubes. ... Additional leaf samples from asymptomatic maize plants that were infested with aphids were collected within Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, North Carolina, and South Dakota in the USA. ... Leaf samples originating from Mexico were collected at varied GPS locations within collection areas shown. ARCHIVE NOTE: all 123 Mexico runs carry a location of the form 'Mexico: Mexico 47', which is a per-sample counter with a country prefix and not a locality; the USA runs do carry real place names. Normalised in lappe_runs.csv, with the original kept in ArchiveLocation. DISCREPANCY: the archive places several USA samples in California (Russell Ranch, Student Farm), which the paper does not list among its USA states.

## location
**94 run(s)** — rule `lappe-location` — 10.1186/s12864-022-09001-w  
*Supplementary Table 1, 'Sup Table S1 Full Sample List' (12864_2022_9001_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx)*

> Per-sample table, 151 rows keyed on 'RNAseq ID' which matches the SRA SampleName exactly, giving Species, Line, Latitude, Longitude and Area. 22 distinct GPS points. Resolves three things the archive got wrong or hid: (1) the archive's organism is Zea mays for the whole project, but the samples are Z. mays 90, Z. mays ssp mexicana 29, Z. mays ssp parviglumis 13, Z. nicaraguensis 8, Z. diploperennis 4, Switchgrass 3, Sorghum bicolor 1 and Aphids 3; (2) the archive's 'Mexico: Mexico 47' style location is a per-sample counter, while the real geography is three collection Areas in Guanajuato with per-sample coordinates; (3) the Line column separates WILD stands from planted material. Retrieved from Springer's static host, static-content.springer.com/esm/..., because Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles zip for PMC9685911 downloads truncated.
